This opening pairing places in relief the vertiginous path Nyong’o charts through a mode of living that “can rear range our perceptions of chronology, time, and temporality” (4). Namely, Blackness. But specifically, the Blackened modes of invention that Nyong’o terms “afro-fabulations”—forms of inventing and reinventing the forgotten, lost, or never known;
that operate as “a queer hack of the codes of an anti-black world
” and “the manner in which gender and sexual norms operate to reproduce systems of racial hierarchy”
(4). These variations on the themes of Black life and living reveal that “the ‘changing same’ of black aesthetics and expressivity may have always already been queer” (4).
